title: ISPA homepage: International Society of Precision Agriculture
answer: The International Society of Precision Agriculture homepage introduces ISPA as a scientific organization developing solutions to feed the world and improve quality of life with new technologies. Its most useful item is that ISPA has developed the Precision Agriculture Definition, available in over fifteen languages. The page also covers membership benefits, a monthly newsletter with job listings and event updates, Country Representatives who connect people, groups and governments to science and experts, and the 17th ICPA and 11th ConBAP planned for summer 2026.

sections.body: This is the homepage of the International Society of Precision Agriculture, also called ISPA. It is published by ISPA itself and works as an organizational landing page rather than a research paper or report. Its scope is introductory, covering the society's mission, membership, newsletter, conferences, Country Representatives and job announcements. The page does not state a publication date, though it mentions the 17th ICPA and 11th ConBAP in summer 2026.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The International Society of Precision Agriculture describes itself as a scientific organization developing solutions to feed the world and improve the quality of life with new technologies. It says it has developed the Precision Agriculture Definition, which is available in over fifteen languages. The page presents ISPA membership as providing exclusive access to membership directories, networking opportunities, discounted conference registrations and more. It also offers a monthly newsletter that sends ISPA news, job listings and upcoming events to an inbox. The society says it is preparing for the 17th ICPA and 11th ConBAP in the summer of 2026, and it directs readers to stay up to date on abstract submission notifications and program updates. Country Representatives are described as helping promote ISPA by championing its mission and purpose globally, especially in the country they represent. ISPA says it is growing internationally and that Country Representatives remain an important position to help ISPA best serve people, groups, governments and others, globally connecting them to science and experts. To become a Country Representative, the page asks interested people to email info@ispag.org with a bio highlighting precision agriculture experience and a CV. It states that all Country Representatives must be current members and links to a membership form. Finally, ISPA members may post job announcements on the website, and these are also included in the newsletters.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text states that ISPA has developed the Precision Agriculture Definition and that it is available in over fifteen languages. It names the 17th ICPA and 11th ConBAP, both scheduled for summer 2026. It says the newsletter is sent monthly. It gives no other figures, dates or numerical results.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in agriculture would use this source to identify ISPA as a scientific organization that connects people, groups and governments to science and experts in precision agriculture. The Precision Agriculture Definition, available in over fifteen languages, may help frame what precision agriculture means, while the conferences, monthly newsletter, job listings and Country Representatives offer ways to follow the field and reach its community. The page does not itself discuss AI, machine learning or specific agricultural AI applications, so it is best treated as an entry point to the precision agriculture community rather than evidence about AI performance or adoption.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Agriculture

sections.body: The page is a short organizational homepage with little substantive detail. It does not cover research methods, findings, data, AI or machine learning, and it gives no publication date. It is published by ISPA itself and serves membership, conference and contact information, so it is partial and not an independent or peer reviewed source. The only dated item is the planned summer 2026 conferences.
